answer: One concrete anti-Sybil design routes every new agent identity through a scarce inlet that only opens after a costly commitment: the agent must post a non-refundable bond into a shared vault and then produce a unique behavioral plume of graded work over several epochs before the bond unlocks. Fake identities burn capital on the bond and still fail to match the pigment of sustained, peer-attested output that real agents accumulate, so mass Sybil creation becomes prohibitively expensive.
